awd_titl_txt: Conference: Hawaii Workshop on Parallel Algorithms and Data Structures
awd_abstract_narration:
This award will support a workshop on Parallel Algorithms and Data Structures at the University of Hawaii, Manoa, March 17-21, 2025. Parallel Algorithms research is an important topic, since parallel computing hardware is omnipresent in many application domains, whether based on multicore processors, graphic processing units (GPUs), or other emerging structures, but most current algorithms research is still following the single-processor sequential model. 

The workshop will bring about 40 researchers together, including 15 doctoral students, to identify, formalize, and attempt to solve problems in parallel algorithms and data structures. It will contribute both to the research progress of the field and the research involvement of the doctoral students. The University of Hawaii is a Pacific-Islander-serving institution in an EPSCoR state.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
1. Summary
The Third Hawaii Workshop on Parallel Algorithms and Data Structures took place on March 17-21, 2025 at the University of Hawaii at Manoa campus. 24 researchers (professors and postdocs) and 11 graduate students attended the workshop.  Funds from NSF were used to support the travel and accommodation of non-local student attendees. There was no registration fee. 

2. Objectives
The workshop was organized with three goals in mind:

  1. Reignite interest in parallel algorithms research.
  2. Bring researchers from wider algorithms community together with researchers in parallel computing.
  3. Promote research in provably-efficient algorithms and data structures for modern parallel architectures.

3. Organizational Structure
The organization of the workshop was modeled after the annual Bellairs Winter Workshop on Computational Geometry and the Dagstuhl series of workshops on Data Structures. 

On the mornings of the first two days of the workshop the workshop participants proposed open problems to work on during the workshop. The afternoons and the last three days were reserved for the participants to work on solving open problems, which were proposed by the participants. At the end of each day, participants presented daily progress of what they have been working on.

4. Outcomes, Dissemination, and Participant Feedback
The workshop started a number of collaborations among the participants. These collaborations led to 10 manuscripts so far,  with one of them already published and three accepted to be published in the coming months.

The feedback about the workshop collected from the participants via a survey was overwhelmingly positive. The average scores to the survey questions on the scale from 1 ("Strongly disagree")  to 5 ("Strongly agree") were:

  • The workshop is beneficial for the parallel algorithms community: 5.0
  • The workshop helped me grow as a researcher/was beneficial for my own research: 4.87
  • I would recommend others to attend: 4.96
  • I got interested/started research in new topics, thanks to participation at this workshop: 4.75

Some of the (anonymous) comments from the survey:

  • "The workshop was by far, the best workshop I have ever been to. I've never gotten that many new collaboration and papers out of a workshop before. I really hope that you will continue doing these workshops." 
  • "The NSF support to students is a nice opportunity that allows them to strengthen their networking and research skills."
  • "Fantastic to work in person with people from different research environments. This workshop will definitely foster future international collaboration"
  • "The workshop was a great opportunity to get junior and senior researchers immersed together working on research problems."
  • "This was the BEST workshop I have ever attended."
  • "This workshop was one of the top few workshops/conferences that I've ever attended in my career..... and I've attended hundreds of them."
